source.note: US label does not state a number. DrugBank-compiled PK summary: 'Bioavailability has been estimated to be above 44%.' Used as a lower-bound point estimate (true absolute bioavailability has not been formally determined in humans per HSDB, which notes only that it exceeds the value seen with incomplete first-pass extraction).

source.citation: DrugBank: Sertraline (DB01104), Volume of Distribution summary, via PubChem CID 68617
source.note: US label does not give a number. DrugBank-compiled PK summary: 'its volume of distribution is estimated to be more than 20 L/kg.' Used as a lower-bound point estimate; HSDB notes direct human Vd has not been formally determined, with animal (rat/dog) data showing >20 L/kg.

source.citation: FDA, 'For Healthcare Professionals | FDA's Examples of Drugs that Interact with CYP Enzymes and Transporter Systems' (content current as of 05/29/2026)
source.note: Table lists sertraline as '2D6 weak inhibitor'. Label 7.1: 'ZOLOFT is a CYP2D6 inhibitor' (no strength).

Radiolabel study: urine 40-45% (no unchanged drug), feces 40-45% 'including 12-14% unchanged sertraline' (midpoints). Feces recorded as bile. MISSING: human bioavailability and Vd are not in the US label, the Zoloft Canada monograph (animal values only) or PubMed abstracts checked.

journey.text: Absorbed slowly from the gut; blood levels peak 4.5 to 8.4 hours after a dose.
Blocks serotonin from being taken back up by nerve cells in the brain, so more serotonin stays active.
Heavily broken down on its first pass through the liver.
Leaves about equally in urine and through the gut, mostly as broken-down pieces.
